prompt: How many competitor price checks were made on each Amsterdam calendar day from 2025-06-28 to 2025-07-04? Use the competitor_prices table and count the checks of both competitors. observed_ts holds the time of the check in UTC: turn it into Amsterdam time first, then take the date, and keep the checks whose Amsterdam date falls in that range, both days included. Return two columns, in this order: check_day, the Amsterdam date, and checks, the number of price checks. Return one row for each day. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the calculated column check_day: the Amsterdam date of each price check.

The hidden test case holds a check at 23:30 UTC on 30 June, which is already 1 July in Amsterdam, 2 hours ahead in summer; the visible checks are all earlier in the day. Convert observed_ts to Amsterdam time before you take the date, in SELECT and in WHERE.
why_this_works: Converting observed_ts to Amsterdam time before taking the date puts a late-evening UTC check on the Amsterdam day it was made.
